clue.text: It is not clear what he has to say

definitions.text: It is not clear what he has to say

parts.words: It is not clear what he has to say
parts.note: reads like a riddle about a secretive or confusing speaker, but describes someone whose speech is indistinct

explanation.surface: A puzzling remark about a man whose message is hard to make out.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who speaks indistinctly, swallowing words, is one whose speech cannot be clearly heard.

clue.text: Gloomy doctor got up

parts.note: MO stands for medical officer, a doctor
rose is the past tense of rise, to get up

explanation.surface: A downcast physician getting out of bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sullen and gloomy is sour-tempered and despondent.

clue.text: Make a note of the time

definitions.meaning: to record in the formal notes of a meeting

explanation.surface: Jotting down what time it is.
explanation.definitionFit: Records of a meeting share the word with the sixty-second unit of time.

clue.text: Rash, comely, upset and inclined to weep

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters are tipped into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone hasty and good-looking, distressed and close to tears.
explanation.definitionFit: Tearful or given to weeping, from the Latin for tear.

clue.text: Sporting body leading doctor a dance

indicators.note: one piece leading means it comes first, before what follows

parts.note: RU is Rugby Union, a sporting body
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree

explanation.surface: A sports official leading a doctor onto the dance floor.
explanation.definitionFit: A Cuban ballroom dance with a lilting rhythm.

clue.text: Dishing out at a lively party

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are thrown out of their order and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone serving food at a lively party.
explanation.definitionFit: A shindig is informal slang for a noisy, lively celebration.

clue.text: Second sanctimonious, ceremonial, religious song

parts.note: pi is informal British for sanctimonious, short for pious
ritual means relating to ceremony

explanation.surface: A list of adjectives for some churchy, solemn singing.
explanation.definitionFit: A religious folk hymn, especially of African American origin.

clue.text: Small amount of news having arrived at the Foreign Office

parts.note: in means arrived, as in the train is in
FO is the abbreviation for the Foreign Office

explanation.surface: A snippet of news reaches the government department for diplomacy.
explanation.definitionFit: A clipped word for information, here a little news.

clue.text: A down-and-out is quite overcome

definitions.meaning: read as two words, totally exhausted

explanation.surface: A tramp who is utterly beaten.
explanation.definitionFit: A lazy idler or vagrant shares the word with the phrase for being utterly exhausted.

clue.text: Odd fellow with perverse sneer in the island

indicators.note: in signals one piece placed inside the other

parts.note: a guy is an odd-looking fellow

indicators.note: perverse means contrary or twisted, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A strange man sneering contrarily on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perverse' turns SNEER into ERNSE, which goes 'in' GUY.
explanation.definitionFit: Guernsey is one of the Channel Islands between England and France.

clue.text: Finnish perhaps written in mystic symbols

definitions.meaning: Finnish poetry was traditionally sung in units called runes, so Finnish verse can be described this way
the old Germanic alphabet of carved characters, credited with magical power

explanation.surface: Wondering whether some Finnish text is written in mysterious symbols.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes both Finnish rune-songs and texts carved in the ancient magical alphabet of the north.

clue.text: General shape of a computer

parts.note: main means chief or general, as in the main body
a frame is the structure or shape of something

explanation.surface: Asking about the overall outline or design of a computer.
explanation.definitionFit: A large central computer serving many terminals is called by this name.

clue.text: Unorthodox Australian revelry

indicators.note: unorthodox means not following the usual pattern, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Wild partying in an unconventional Australian style.
explanation.walkthrough: The Roman winter festival of Saturn was famous for licence and feasting, giving its name to any riotous celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: Any wild, unrestrained celebration takes its name from the riotous ancient Roman festival.

clue.text: Outside broadcast on a northern port

parts.note: OB is the standard abbreviation for an outside broadcast, a programme filmed away from the studio

explanation.surface: A television crew filming on location at a harbour town in the north.
explanation.walkthrough: OBAN is a ferry port on the west coast of Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Oban is a harbour town in western Scotland, a port for ferries to the Hebrides.

clue.text: Estimate of men's assets varied

indicators.note: varied means changed, so the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Valuing what a group of men own in various ways.
explanation.definitionFit: An evaluation or judgment of value, as in a tax valuation.

clue.text: No professional players here?

parts.note: asks where one finds only unpaid performers, the theatre of enthusiasts rather than paid actors

explanation.surface: A question about a place without professional athletes or performers.
explanation.definitionFit: Theatre put on by unpaid enthusiasts has no professional actors among its cast.

clue.text: Devised even if put incorrectly

parts.note: though means even if

indicators.note: incorrectly means put the wrong way, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A plan was devised even if it was set down wrongly.
explanation.definitionFit: To invent or conceive a scheme is to devise it.

clue.text: Dutch port or gin

definitions.meaning: a harbour town near Rotterdam in the Netherlands
a Dutch juniper spirit named after that town

explanation.surface: Asking whether a Dutch harbour or a spirit is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: A port town near Rotterdam gave its name to a style of Dutch gin, genever.

clue.text: Can't this be tied tight?

parts.note: suggests a knot that will not hold fast, because it is designed to run along the rope

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about something that will not fasten.
explanation.definitionFit: A running knot that slides along the cord, so it cannot be fixed tight.

clue.text: Deliberately unfriendly treatment from unheated joint perhaps

definitions.meaning: the idiom for snubbing someone on purpose
literally a cut of meat from the upper foreleg served cold

explanation.surface: Being snubbed, compared to being served a cold cut of meat.
explanation.definitionFit: To snub someone is an idiom; literally a chilled shoulder cut of lamb or pork is a joint of meat.

clue.text: Sneeze, say, then use this

parts.note: the sound of a sneeze, atishoo, imitates the two words that name what you then reach for

explanation.surface: Advice to grab a handkerchief after sneezing.
explanation.definitionFit: A paper handkerchief is what one uses to wipe the nose.

clue.text: Allow an instruction to be given to the hairdresser

definitions.text: an instruction to be given to the hairdresser
definitions.meaning: read as two words, asking for the hair to be curled with a perm

explanation.surface: Permission to tell the stylist what to do.
explanation.definitionFit: To let something happen is to authorise it; a perm is a lasting hair curl.

clue.text: Admits Greek character in Zulu regiment

annotationWithheld.clue: Admits Greek character in Zulu regiment

clue.text: Showing energy and initiative making the first attack

definitions.meaning: describes a forceful, go-getting approach, as in business
describes a hostile party that strikes first

explanation.surface: Praise for a bold competitor who strikes first.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both pushy, enterprising drive and hostility that starts a fight.

clue.text: It is soundly similar at the end

definitions.text: It is soundly similar at the end

parts.words: It is soundly similar at the end
parts.note: describes words whose final sounds match, as in verse

explanation.surface: A remark about something that matches in tone at its close.
explanation.definitionFit: Words that share the same ending sound, as in poetry.

clue.text: Express a desire, well, often granted here

definitions.text: Express a desire, well, often granted here

parts.words: Express a desire, well, often granted here
parts.note: to express a desire is the verb, and the well where desires are granted is the ... well

explanation.surface: Making a hope known at a well where hopes come true.
explanation.definitionFit: To long for something, the act associated with the wishing well.

clue.text: The art of an oral examiner

definitions.text: The art of an oral examiner

parts.words: The art of an oral examiner
parts.note: an oral examiner seems to set spoken exams, but here looks inside mouths

explanation.surface: The skill of someone who tests students in a spoken exam.
explanation.definitionFit: Inspecting and treating teeth is the profession of the person who examines mouths.

clue.text: Nonsense poems found on the race-course

indicators.note: nonsense suggests the letters are jumbled into a different arrangement

explanation.surface: Nonsense verses discovered at a racing venue.
explanation.walkthrough: EPSOM, in Surrey, is the English racecourse that hosts the Derby.
explanation.definitionFit: Epsom Downs in Surrey is a famous horse-racing venue, home of the Derby.

clue.text: Fit when the game has finished

definitions.meaning: read as two words, the contest is over

explanation.surface: Saying something suits once play is over.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that correspond fit together; a contest that is over has ended.

clue.text: In the shopping centre a tramp will beg

indicators.note: in signals the letters lie inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A vagrant asks for money in a mall.
explanation.definitionFit: To plead earnestly with someone is to implore or beg.
